newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. fires 25-30 missiles on south Iraq - official.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fires 25-30 missiles on south Iraq - official.

text.p: U.S. navy warships in the Gulf and B-52 bombers fired 25 to 30 cruise missiles on military targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday, a Western defence official in the Middle East said.
He told Reuters between 25 and 30 missiles were fired on southern Iraq from two navy warships in the Gulf and two B-52 bombers.
The official named the warships as the USS Laboon guided missile destroyer and the USS Shilo cruiser.
He said the missiles "hit air defence targets in the southern part of Iraq, surface-to-air missile sites and air defence radar installations".
The attack started between 0415 and 0430 GMT, the official said. He would not comment on damage inflicted on the Iraqi targets nor say whether the attack had stopped.
The Pentagon in Washington had earlier said the attack, ordered by President Bill Clinton, was in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds in the north.
U.S. officials said on Monday Iraqi President Saddam Hussein must be made to pay for ignoring U.S. warnings and launching weekend attacks against Kurds north of the 36th parallel in his country.

In Baghdad, residents said air raid sirens had blared in parts of the Iraqi capital on Tuesday but were not heard all over the city. Witnesses said anti-aircraft fire was launched from positions in Baghdad, but it was not immediately clear what the fire was aimed at.
An Iraqi television channel run by Saddam's son Uday confirmed the U.S. strikes against Iraq.

The United States had stationed warships armed with highly-accurate Tomahawk cruise missiles in the Gulf and moved B-52 bombers carrying air-launched cruise missiles to Guam in the Pacific. The B-52s can fly non-stop into missile range several hundred miles from Iraq.
The $1.2 million ship-launched Tomahawks can fly unmanned nearly 700 miles (1,120 km) and strike targets with high accuracy.

The White House believes Saddam sent three tank divisions composed of 30,000-40,000 elite Republican Guard troops into northern Iraq over the weekend to help a Kurdish faction involved in a bloody power struggle with another Kurdish group linked to Iran.
